summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of severe Crohn’s disease, status post multiple abdominal surgeries including colectomy and ileostomy takedown, was admitted with worsening abdominal pain and decreased stool frequency following a Tysabri infusion. Imaging revealed findings concerning for a partial small bowel obstruction, likely due to a combination of inflammatory stricture and adhesions. He was managed conservatively with bowel rest, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and pain control. His renal function improved from acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. Anxiety was managed with quetiapine after lorazepam was discontinued due to confusion. MR enterography confirmed stable active inflammation in the distal ileum without abscess or stricture. Pain resolved, diet was advanced, and he was discharged home on Percocet for breakthrough pain, continued prednisone and Tysabri, with follow-up arranged.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
